name: Pinochle Single Deck Partnership
description: Pinochle with single 48-card deck; four players in partnerships. Melding and trick-taking.

overview.description: Pinochle with single 48-card deck; four players in partnerships. Melding and trick-taking.

history.origins: Partnership pinochle shares the same roots as pinochle generally: either as a cousin of Binokel with both evolving from bezique, or from the Swiss and South German game Binocle or Binokel. German immigrants brought Binokel to America in the last quarter of the 19th century, where it was mispronounced and misspelled as 'pinochle'; it became a favorite among American Jewish and Irish immigrants. Partnership auction pinochle emerged as the standard form in the United States in the early 20th century.
timeline: Late 19th century: German immigrants brought Binokel to America; game became known as pinochle. Early 20th century: partnership auction pinochle popular in the United States.

setup.deck: 48-card Pinochle deck: twelve cards per suit (two each of 9, 10, Jack, Queen, King, Ace) in all four French suits.
setup.dealing: All 48 cards dealt clockwise in packets of three or four, starting with the player to the dealer's left (eldest hand). Each player receives 12 cards. Deal rotates clockwise each hand.
setup.equipment: Standard 48-card Pinochle deck (two copies of 9 through Ace in each suit).

rules.objective: Reach the agreed target score (typically 1000 or 1500) by combining meld points and trick points. Bid to name trump; the bidding team must make at least their bid (meld plus trick points) or be set.
rules.gameplay: Deal 12 cards each. Auction: players bid in turn; high bidder declares trump. All players meld (runs, marriages, pinochles, arounds); points counted. High bidder leads; follow suit if possible, must trump if void; identical cards rank first-played. Trick points plus meld must meet or exceed the bid for the bidding team. First partnership to reach target wins.

scoring.description: Meld points (runs, marriages, pinochles, arounds, dix) plus trick points (aces and tens 10 each, kings and queens 5 each, last trick 10). Bidding team must make at least their bid or be set (bid subtracted).
scoring.winCondition: First partnership to reach the agreed target score (typically 1000 or 1500) wins the game.
